answer: Sponsor-backed reputation bonds make a sybil attack expensive. Every new agent identity must post a collateral bond that a sponsor vouches for, and identities caught misbehaving get their bond slashed, which also burns the sponsor's standing. A tundra-sized fleet of cheap accounts then costs real capital to run, while the kernel of trust stays with bonded, sponsored peers. An atlas of sponsor links lets the network spot clusters that share one funding source.
